{{Short description|Construction used in 4-dimensional topology}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''grope''' is a construction used in [[4-dimensional topology]], introduced by {{harvtxt|Štan'ko|1971}} and named by {{harvtxt|Cannon|1978}} "because of its multitudinous fingers".  Capped gropes were used by {{harvtxt|Freedman|1984}} as a substitute for [[Casson handle]]s, that (unlike Casson handles) work better for [[simply connected space|non-simply-connected]] [[4-manifold]]s. 

A capped surface in a 4-manifold is roughly a surface together with some 2-disks, called caps, whose boundaries [[Generating set of a group|generate]] the [[fundamental group]] of the surface.  A capped grope is obtained by repeatedly replacing the caps of a capped surface by another capped surface.  Capped surfaces and capped  gropes are studied in {{harvtxt|Freedman|Quinn|1990}}.
